Report Details
Inspection Client: MINARD RUN OIL CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/22/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8259795
Permit API: 053-26767
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/22/2025
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone call made by Dan McCamey, of Minard Run Oil Company (MROC) on December 22, 2025. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred at Warrant 5107 Well #25P (API# 053-26767). A failure in the buried steel pipeline leading to this well resulted in leaking crude oil rising to the surface. A well tender spotted the crude oil earlier today and notified MROC immediately. A work crew arrived soon thereafter to repair the line, install containment, and begin remediating the released crude oil. Upon my arrival to the site, the pipeline had been repaired which stopped the release. The released crude oil had migrated down the road ditch for approximately 20 feet, across the road through a culvert, flowing downhill into a spring, ultimately entering Guiton Run (HQ-CWF) at (41.513992, -79.18582) after traveling approximately 50 yards. Pockets of weathered crude oil and emulsion were evident downstream for approximately 475 yards ending at (41.512156, -79.189991). The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident was unknown due to the lack of accumulated product at the site. At this time, it is estimated that less than one barrel of product was released. A siphon dam was installed in the road ditch, beyond the direction of flow where the crude oil was initially spotted. A second siphon dam was installed and lined beyond the road culvert. Booms and diapers were already placed on the surface and at the point of entry in Guiton Run. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. Additional booms and diapers should be placed in Guiton Run to absorb and capture any released crude oil within the stream. The stream should be continuously monitored until there is no longer any evidence of crude oil. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor remediation of this release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will need to be conducted to verfiy that the cleanup is deemed complete prior to any seeding/mulching. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The conventional well was equipped for production with a pump jack. The well name, API number, and operator information were displayed on a sign attached to the pump jack.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 931182
Permit API: 081-21461
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Eldred Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/28/2021
Comments: On September 28, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow inspection to a reported spill at the Inflection Energy TLC Well Pad. The spill notification was received on September 26, 2021. The DEP met with Inflection Energy Zac Subra found an area of about 50 ft x 80 ft with variable conductivity levels from 1,200 uS/cm to 10,000 u/S/cm. The location of the spill was N 41.3335434, W -76.9287938. Inflection began excavation immediately. Upon arrival, the area of impact had been excavated and backfilled. The spill did not appear to leave the pad surface. The spill was caused by a hole in the containment and a leak in a flushing line used during the well stimulation process. An estimated volume of the leak will be determined when the remainder of the rig mats are removed and the area under the mats can be evaluated. Penn E&R collected confirmatory samples on September 27, 2021. Inflection Energy is in the process of setting up for flow back on the recently stimulated wells. The MASS and freshwater AST still remain on site. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The DEP recommends beginning the Act 2 process when the rig mats are completely removed due to the unknown volume of the spill.

Comments: On May 15, 2024 the Department conducted a follow up inspection of EQTs Cook Unit 17H well pad in response to IR 3747032 where violations were issued for failure to maintain PCSM BMPs. At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was present at the entrance of the access road which appeared stabilized and the ERP was present in the on-site mailbox. There are two wells on this pad that appeared to be equipped for production and are surrounded by cement barriers. Well 17H has it's well tag present with all necessary information posted, and no fluid discharges or fluid leaks were observed from/near the wellhead. The 17H GPU was surrounded by cement barriers and was not in secondary containment however, well 17H has a SPUD date prior to the October 2016 proclamation of chapter 78a, therefore secondary containment is not required to be installed. The 17H production tank was in secondary containment that had fluid pooled in it and was surrounded by cement barriers. The production tank appeared to be equipped for production with no observable fluid leaks or fluid discharge coming from it. The Department is again recommend the Operator continue to monitor the secondary containment to ensure that fluid currently in it will not inhibit its 110% hold capacity requirements. Upon inspection of the perimeter of the well site, at least 70% vegetative growth was seen throughout, as well as two riprap aprons. The riprap apron at the front of the well site did not show any erosion or sedimentation concerns, however the riprap apron at the rear of the well site (where violations were initially issued for during IR 3747032) still appears to be in violation. It is apparent that some riprap was added to the outlet and that some seeding/mulching was done by the appearance of vegetation looking fuller behind the riprap outlet, but pooling of fluid and saturated grass can be seen directly behind the riprap outlet and follows the channel that was once leading to the agricultural field behind the well site. While on site, the department contacted Jeremy Barber a representative of EQT to let them know that the riprap apron is still failing to prevent channelize flow from occurring. Jeremy stated that they will be sending an NOV response on May 16, 2024 notating that some maintenance was done and that they plan to continue to monitor it. Jeremy also stated that EQT would beef up the riprap apron some more to hopefully prevent this channelize flow from continuing to occur, and is going to think of a way to further prevent this without effecting all the grass surrounding the well site. Jeremy will set up a walk through of the well site with the Department after more maintenance is done on the riprap outlet.Based on todays inspection, violations issued under IR 3747032 will remain outstanding for failure to maintain PCSM BMPs.

Comments: On March 16, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Ziolkowoski Well Site (NOT approved on 11/6/2023) in regard to a release reported to the Department on 3/15/2026 (CTS 395839). Present during the inspection was operator representative Nick Reda.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, there are 14 total wells on the well pad. Wells (2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H, 9H, 1H,10H,11H,12H, and 14H) appeared equipped for production with well tags present. Mr. Reda stated they are currently swapping out equipment to complete flowback operations on the 13H.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks and GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Reda guided the Department to the location(s) of the reported release. According to Mr. Reda the release occurred on 3/15/2026. He stated the release was caused by a scrubber malfunction on a third-party water truck. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of produced water released to the graveled access road.The Department observed the location(s) of the release and remediation. It appeared the area of the release was split into two different sections of the access road. Mr. Reda said due to the malfunction of the scrubber on the water truck, the release occurred only on the steep portions of the access road. Therefore, the release began approximately halfway down the access road, ceased as the truck reached a level area, and then continued to release on another steep section towards the bottom of the access road.Upon inspection of where the release began, the Department observed an area where impacted material was excavated from the access road (photos 12-13). According to Mr. Reda, the release in this area of the access road was about 150 feet in length and about 1 foot in width. Small puddles of rainwater were observed in this section of the access road. Conductivity readings of 0.49mS, 0.24mS, and 0.43mS, were obtained in the area of the release/remediation. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.60mS obtained in the gravel on the side of the access road near the well pad entrance (away from the spill and heavy vehicle traffic). Prior to leaving the site, the area of excavation was backfilled with clean gravel (Photos 23-24).Upon inspection of where the release continued near the bottom of the access road, the Department observed fresh gravel (Photo 17). Mr. Reda stated the impacted material had been removed and the area of excavation had been backfilled. Mr. Reda stated the release in the area of the access road was about 180 feet in length and about 1 foot in width. Conductivity readings of 0.12mS, 0.15mS, and 0.23mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.60mS obtained.Mr. Reda stated all impacted material was placed into 3 roll-off boxes (photos 21-22) and would be disposed of properly. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued as immediately corrected for the observed release as it appeared to be remediated in accordance with current regulations (78a66).

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8233663
Permit API: 125-27893
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Amwell Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/14/2025
Comments: On 05/14/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Cogar Well Site following an incident report received by the Department on 05/12/2025 (CTS 389093). SPSI crew on site remediating. The operator reported a spill to the Department on 05/13/2025 regarding more than 5 gallons of production water that were released on a load out pumpkin. No waterways were affected. The incident occurred on 05/12/2025 and reported over two hours after the incident on 05/13/2025. The following was observed:The area of impact was adjacent to the containment of the production tanks. SPSI excavated the impacted area to determine the extent of impact and place waste in roll off dumpsters. The area of impact was under the load out pumpkin and where the cement containment would be. A portion of the dump line was exposed during excavation. Water was pooling within the excavated area (Photos 1-6).Conductivity readings were taken within the area of impact. Readings were 5.23, 7.60, 13.62, 14.27, 16.22 mS/cm, and Over Range (Photos 7-14).Additional readings taken within the upper layers of substrate and clay layer were 430, 533, 850, and 968 uS/cm (Photos 15-18).The cement containment had a reading of Over Range. There appeared to be residual fluid combined with rainwater (Photo 19).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan were on site (Photo 20).Due to the release of production fluid greater than 5 gallons and failure to report a reportable spill within 2 hours, violations of 78a54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), 78a66(b)2 are being issued. The Department requests an updated estimation of the quantity of production fluid released. The Department requests information on if the operator intends to remediate per Act 2 guidelines regarding the quantity released.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up inspection of the Tilden Marcellus - Thomas 808 well pad located in Elk Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/9/2019 @1015 hours. The weather was 72 degrees and sunny, humidity 73%, no wind. Activity onsite consists of Tilden Marcellus finishing plumbing in the recently completed wells and removing the temporary flow back equipment. Jenn Compton and Taylor Parsons, Tilden Marcellus/Rockdale were present onsite for the inspection. As of today's inspection most of the secondary containment and rig mats have been removed. Tilden Marcellus is currently performing screening and removal of pad material impacted by stimulation activities, and the reported release on 6/3/2019. Ms. Compton stated in addition to the eastern pad edge and fill slope, an area in the center of the pad was found to have material with an elevated conductivity. The removed material was observed stockpiled in secondary containment, and covered in tarps. Trucks were observed removing fluid from the tank farm located along the northern cut slope. Fluid with an elevated conductivity was observed in both layers of secondary containment. A puddle/muddy area against the foam berm (photo#6) had a field measured conductivity of 3.28mS/cm. Mr. Parsons was notified of my findings regarding the tank farm. He stated a site truck was being dispatched to clean out the containments, and additional containment would be constructed in the truck load area to prevent spills to the ground surface from hose breaks. Violations of 25 Pa Code 78a.57a and SWMA 610(2) cited 6/17/2019 in IR#2894467, due to the operation of an illegal waste transfer station, are CORRECTED at this time. Tilden Marcellus ceased hauling and storage of fluids when notified of the violations. A NOV response was received on 7/9/2019. Violations of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301 and 25 Pa Code 78a56(a), cited 6/4/2019 in IR#2889847, remain OUTSTANDING against API#117-20478 from a previous release. Site remediation is ongoing. Once a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEP's Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review, and attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed, the outstanding violations will be closed. No additional violations are cited at this time. Please ensure any deficiencies noted are addressed and contact me with any questions. I departed the site at 1130 hours.

Comments: On April 2, 2024, inspection conducted Brownlee Kelley 12333 well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County. This inspection follows up to IR 3737318, which was conducted in response to a spill that occurred the day prior. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on August 6, 2021.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Heavy sedimentation was observed in the access road, with accelerated erosion rills observed in the access road closer to the well pad (see photos 2 and 3). However, the Department did not observe it entering off-site Waters of the Commonwealth. Flowback equipment and related secondary containment was removed from site, as well as the rolloff dumpsters containing the impacted material (see photo 4). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 5). All other machinery and primary containments that appear to contain regulated substances were placed within secondary containment. GPU units onsite were either placed within secondary containment or equipped with interconnected vertical separators (see photo 6). The area formerly impacted by the spill documented in IR 3737318 and IR 3736812 was freshly backfilled with no elevated conductivity detected (see photos 7-10). The ERP was onsite (see photo 10). Well 4H was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 13 and 14). There are eight other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 12).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the operator conduct immediate repairs to the access road in a manner that abates the aforementioned accelerated erosion and heavy sedimentation, and prevents it from worsening. Violations issued under IR 3737318 shall remain outstanding, as the NOI to Remediation of the release under Act 2 requirements have not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB Program. Additional violations are being issued against the accelerated erosion and heavy sedimentation observed in the access road.

The well posting was present at the time of the inspection.The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the affected area of the pump jack fluid release documented in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. There were erosion and sedimentation issues at the well site and adjacent to the wellhead due to the prior releases of the fluid from the pump jack onto the ground in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. It appears the erosion that previously extended adjacent to and downslope from the well site is now exhibiting greater than 70% vegetative coverage with the exception of the area between the agricultural fence adjacent to the well site and the wellhead ;this area is located approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead. A background soil conductivity reading was taken. The soil conductivity reading was 0.0370mS. Soil conductivity readings were taken around the wellhead. The soil conductivity readings were 0.883mS, 0.273mS, 0.407mS, and 0.464mS. Although soil conductivity readings around the wellhead with visually stained gravel were lower compared to previous inspections, these readings are still higher than the background soil conductivity reading. It appears visually that the area around the wellhead and area extending approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead are not remediated due to the stained gravel, the lack of vegetation, and high conductivity readings.The area between the agricultural fence adjacent to the well site and the wellhead ;this area is located approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead had soil conductivity readings of 4.71mS and 5.46mS. The Department again requests the following information for both spills; evaluate the release that has occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred, to be provided in the requested NOV response by August 9, 2024. The Department also requests waste manifests upon proper disposal of wastes generated from the spill remediation.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.Soil conductivity calibration was conducted on August 6 2024 at 14:22.

Comments: Merchbaker was on site to investigate a reported brine release to containment called into the Department by Lola Energy Partners (Lola) Vice President Jayson Johnson.Lola reported approximately 100 barrels of brine was released to containment and that representatives were on site to being the clean up process.When Merchbaker arrived there was a vac truck on site removing brine from inside containment and a Lola representative was waiting. Upon talking to the Lola representative, the cause of the release was a schedule 40 90 fitting had rotted out after years of contact with the brine. Lola represetitivies replaced the faulty fitting and conducted a mechanical assessment of all other fittings on pad. Clean up of containment will continue in the coming days with contractors coming to deep clean containment and properly dispose of contaminated materials. Merchbaker requested disposal receipts for all removed materials. During the inspection, Merchbaker notoced bubbling coming from under one of the ASTs. The Lola representitive stated that they keep positive pressure on the tanks, and stated that this particular tank had been shut down and not used for years. Merchbaker requested an inquiry into this tank to repair possible damage and/or remove the unused equipment. Merchbaker will continue to monitor this location as the clean up continues.
